description: The reuse ledger cannot move without a trace line: sync refuses a cache it cannot verify, a reuse appends the trace before the registry moves, and a deterministic append-boundary failure (EISDIR directory-swap, privilege-independent) leaves the registry byte-identical.
notes: rcos-eval/2: this package declares NO adapter of its own. It names the registered
capability and the input document, and the run reaches the capability through the
invocation kernel — `rcos run reuse-ledger` takes the identical path. The thing
being evaluated is the thing reuse will call; there is no second way to invoke it.
Version 2 replaces the chmod-0444 read-only fixture: the capability adapter now
moves the trace log aside and puts a directory at its path, so the real
`rcos reuse-log` is refused at open(2) with EISDIR for EVERY uid (root bypasses
DAC mode bits, not file-type checks) — the same invariant, proven under both
privilege levels, with the original log restored byte-for-byte.
The gates read $RCOS_INVOCATION_DIR/output.json (the observation the kernel froze)
and re-hash the evidence beside it, so a claim its own bytes contradict fails.
